newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom in decoder plan-paper.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom in decoder plan-paper.

text.p: Germany's newly-privatised Deutsche Telekom AG is holding talks with a range of groups on the development of a decoder for digital television over cable networks, German newspaper Welt am Sonntag reported on Sunday.
The talks include German television channels ARD and ZDF, the Austrian broadcaster ORF, electronics groups Grundig, Philips, Sony and Thomson, the paper said, quoting an ZDF official.

Digital TV technology permits a greater number of TV channels to be broadcasted than through conventional means and also allows broadcasters more easily to charge viewers for those programmes they choose to watch.
The new decoders are due to come onto the market by the end of August at the latest and cost at least 600-800 marks, the ZDF official said.
Telekom was also said to be keen to become a broadcaster of television to its cable customers, which currently numbers some 16.7 million households.
At present, only the Munich-based Kirch group offers digital television in Germany.
